name: Strike
description: A basic physical blow. No resource cost.

name: Guard Stance
description: Brace. Sharply raises defense but only briefly.

name: Rush Barrage
description: A dense flurry of close-range strikes.

name: Tempo Halt
description: Freezes the flow of the battle for every opponent.

name: Restore
description: Reverts an ally's wounds. Enough to buy a turn, not enough to undo one.

name: Emerald Snare
description: Ranged binding attack that slows the target. Power 75 sits below the free basic attack, so for Kakyoin's atk 78 this trades damage away for the slow rather than adding one to the other; see the riposte note and the issue it points at.

name: Emerald Splash
description: Scatters a burst of psychic emeralds across the enemy line.

name: Blade Volley
description: Scatters throwing blades across the enemy line. Thrown by the handful, into a moment that is not moving.

name: Sun Flare
description: A searing burst of heat that leaves the target bleeding heat.

name: Concussive Slam
description: A heavy blow that can stagger the target outright.

name: Riposte
description: Answers the blow before it lands. The cut is shallow; the habit it breaks is not. Power shipped at 85 and measured at 0 wins in 300: because damage subtracts half the target's defence, any power below the basic attack's 100 is a downgrade the AI's scorer cannot see, since it prices the debuff separately and generously. 110 is the least that makes a paid skill worth more than the free one it displaces.

name: Flurry Cut
description: Two shallow cuts in the time one blow would take. Power is 105 and not lower on purpose: damage subtracts half the target's defence, so anything under the free attack's 100 is a downgrade, which is the fault riposte shipped with and #33 records. The point of the skill is tempo_cost 700 against the basic attack's 1000 - the first content here that uses tempo as a design lever rather than copying the default. Note that the scorer has no term for tempo_cost, so the AI cannot see the property this skill exists for.

name: Wither Hex
description: Lays a weakening mark on every opponent at once. The first skill in this file that deals no damage of any kind, which is the point and also the risk: the harness counts a combatant inert when it deals no damage and heals nothing, so its carrier has to hold skill.strike too or a debuffer doing its job perfectly would be reported as having sat out the batch. Potency is 26 and not 40 because damage subtracts half the target's defence after multiplying by attack, so an attack debuff bites harder than its percentage - at 40 the same emerald_splash falls from 48 to 11, a 77% cut, which deletes Kakyoin rather than trimming him. Same asymmetry as the riposte note, seen from the other side. Duration is 3, and the way it got back to 3 is the useful part of this entry. It shipped at 3 and the encounter measured 92% against a band of 58..86, which was diagnosed as the hex barely landing. That diagnosis was wrong and is retracted here. It rested on party damage per battle, which cannot show a debuff at all: in a fixture the party usually wins, that figure is pinned to the foe HP pool, 1179 against a pool of 1180 and later 1256 against 1260. The quantity that can show a debuff is damage per ACTION, and it said the hex was already cutting 17-24% at duration 3. Duration was then raised to 8 anyway, and it was inert - Jotaro improved 5%, Kakyoin got marginally worse, and the whole gain belonged to the hit points raised in the same commit. The reason duration saturates is that it counts in the BEARER's own turns, which battle.rs tick_statuses does by decrementing only the acting combatant's statuses: Jotaro takes about nine turns a battle, the Weaver lands about three hexes, so 3 already covers nearly all the turns that follow the first one, and the turns before the first hex can never be covered by any duration whatsoever. The ceiling is (turns - 1) / turns, about 89%, and 3 was already close to it. What actually fixed the encounter was hit points, twice, 480 to 560 to 690, because for a debuffer HP is an uptime knob and not a durability knob. One consequence to keep in mind if this is ever tuned again: at 3 the scorer gives 100 * 26/100 * 3 = 78, and with only one party member left 78 * 85/100 = 66 falls below a free strike's 100, so the carrier correctly goes back to hitting things - a branch that duration 8 suppressed. And one thing this skill proved about the engine rather than about itself: the Weaver's accuracy rolls came to exactly its strike uses, 295 against 295 and later 370 against 370, so a status-only skill draws no accuracy roll at all.
